title: Profile overview
text: Sachin Ved Gupta is a McMaster University Software Engineering Co-op student focused on applied AI systems, AI agents, machine-learning infrastructure, simulations, developer tools, and product-oriented software. His recurring pattern is to take messy operational or human context, model it clearly, and build software that helps people make decisions or complete work. He has completed software engineering and data science internships at Nokia, Nokia Bell Labs, Shopify, Zipline, and Microsoft. He is strongest when connecting ML or agent technology to a concrete workflow rather than building a model demo in isolation.

title: Career throughline
text: Across Sachin's work, the same design instinct appears: model a complex environment, expose the right interface, and let software help a person act. At Nokia, that meant infrastructure provisioning and diagnosis. At Nokia Bell Labs, it meant grounding ML and agent systems in engineering knowledge and operational signals. At Shopify, it meant production recommendation infrastructure and debugging. At Zipline, it meant simulating an autonomous delivery network and making the simulator accessible through natural language. At Microsoft, it meant improving PowerPoint Web boot reliability and prototyping repeatable browser-agent testing. Student work extends the same pattern through browser agents, autonomous drones, educational agents, cloud provisioning, and AI-assisted storytelling.

title: McMaster Software Engineering education
text: Sachin is pursuing a Bachelor of Software Engineering Co-op at McMaster University from September 2023 through an expected April 2028 graduation. His learning spans software design, systems, algorithms, machine learning, compilers, cloud systems, and product development. He has a 3.9 out of 4.0 cumulative GPA and earned a perfect 4.0 in first year.

title: Academic achievements and scholarships
text: Sachin earned a Provost's Honour Roll Medal, a perfect first-year 4.0, and approximately $10,000 in scholarships from OpenText and Rogers. These achievements reflect sustained academic performance and early external recognition.

title: Microsoft — Software Engineering Intern
text: At Microsoft in Vancouver from May through August 2026, Sachin worked as a Software Engineering Intern on the PowerPoint Web Performance team. He shipped boot and reliability fixes involving canvas centering, off-slide shape visibility, scroll behavior, comments-pane layout reservation, and visual popping. He also built a PR-aware browser-agent testing prototype that compared baseline and changed builds across realistic tasks and environments, producing recordings and reproducible issue reports. Across a seven-day run, the work identified 17 optimizations; his internship results included 21 percent faster boot time and 13 production fixes.
source_name: Career profile and public-safe Microsoft case study

title: Zipline — Data Science Intern
text: From January through April 2026, Sachin worked as a Data Science Intern at Zipline. He built a natural-language Codex workflow around an operations simulator: the agent could generate configurations, run scenarios, return charts, explain results, and suggest follow-up analysis. Under that interface, he built an extensible discrete-event simulation of autonomous-delivery operations, modelling aircraft, charging docks, workers, partners, event timing, demand, weather, and failures. He calibrated the simulation with historical data and built validation tooling for throughput, timing, utilization, and bottleneck diagnosis. The project combined an LLM agent with rigorous simulation, data calibration, developer tooling, visualization, and cross-functional decision support.
source_name: Career profile and confidentiality-safe Zipline case study

title: Shopify — Software Engineering Intern
text: From September through December 2025, Sachin worked in Shopify's Recommendations Infrastructure and Shop app context. He built systems for recommendation relevance, production ML inference and streaming, debugging, and multi-tier caching using Triton, Apache Flink, Kafka, GCP, Bigtable, and DSPy. He distilled a relevancy judge to a one-billion-parameter model for more than ten million recommendations, built recommendation debugging used by more than 80 engineers, and created local-to-remote-to-Bigtable caching that made an advertised-product filtering path 11 times faster.

title: Nokia Bell Labs — Machine Learning Intern
text: From April through August 2025, Sachin was a Machine Learning Intern at Nokia Bell Labs. He researched generative AI and predictive modelling for 5G and network workloads, and built retrieval and knowledge-graph systems over engineering sources such as JIRA issues, logs, and code. The work used LangChain, Pinecone, Neo4j, and LangGraph. He also developed agents that detected application failures and executed Linux recovery actions. The role connected research, knowledge representation, RAG, agents, and operational reliability.

title: Nokia — Software Engineering Intern
text: From April through August 2024, Sachin worked as a Software Engineering Intern at Nokia. He automated OpenStack virtual-machine provisioning with modular Python and Bash, built a Chrome-based log-analysis and status-visualization tool, worked across Linux and infrastructure APIs, and delivered a four-hour technical training session to roughly 65 experienced employees. His automation reduced manual provisioning effort by 98.3 percent and bug-resolution time by 64 percent.

title: McMaster Aerial Robotics — software and ML leadership
text: Sachin is a founding member and Software Team Lead with McMaster Aerial Robotics. He led a roughly 20-person ML subteam working toward autonomous-drone competition goals. His technical work spans object detection, inference optimization, simulation, flight-controller integration, infrared detection, triangulation, SLAM and LiDAR, dashboards, and edge deployment. The role combines architecture across software, ML, sensors, and hardware with mentoring and team coordination.

title: GDG McMaster — Open Source Team Lead
text: As an Open Source Team Lead with GDG or GDSC McMaster, Sachin led roughly ten developers building InterfaceAI, a declarative browser agent with planning, memory, DOM-first perception, computer-vision fallback, orchestration, and a browser or web interface. As Project Lead, he provided technical direction, organized agile execution, mentored developers, guided documentation, and shaped the overall agent-system design.

title: McMaster Rocketry — Payload Software
text: With McMaster Rocketry's payload software team, Sachin contributed to low-latency Wi-Fi communication, 360-degree camera processing, microcontroller integrations, and software around liquid-metal electronics experiments. The Sparrow payload combined a 360-degree camera and recovery beacon, flew on Nimbus, and helped the team win the Payload Challenge at Launch Canada 2025.
source_name: Career profile and McMaster Rocketry public pages

title: McMaster SumoBots
text: Sachin built an autonomous sumo robot and helped run a competition for more than 100 participants through McMaster SumoBots. His robot achieved a 4–2 competitive record. The experience demonstrates ownership, embedded programming, event execution, and practical robotics under time and reliability constraints.

title: StoryBook Memoirs
text: StoryBook Memoirs is a conversational family-storytelling product Sachin built to interview elders, structure their memories, and turn them into an editable illustrated book, with voice-oriented interaction and export. It is one of his strongest founder projects because the AI serves a clear human purpose: preserving family stories. The product has a public working application and is a leading current startup direction.

title: InterfaceAI browser agent
text: InterfaceAI is an open-source browser agent that Sachin led through GDG McMaster. It executes declarative tasks through planning, memory, DOM-first interaction, computer-vision fallback, orchestration, and a Chrome or web interface. It demonstrates agent architecture as a complete system spanning perception, state, action, and recovery.

title: NKI Llama inference optimization
text: In the NKI Llama project, Sachin reimplemented transformer operations for AWS Trainium using the Neuron Kernel Interface and achieved a 1.13-times latency speedup. The project demonstrates lower-level ML-systems and performance work: understanding transformer computation, mapping operations to accelerator primitives, measuring latency, and balancing readability with hardware-aware optimization.

title: LearnBridge educational agent
text: LearnBridge is an educational agent Sachin built with Google ADK and ReAct-style reasoning, connected to Google Classroom and Calendar workflows. It helps students gather course context, extract assignment concepts, organize deadlines, and start assignments faster through multi-agent planning, memory, and real tools. The project reduced assignment-start time by 80 percent and saved students an average of two hours per week.

title: StockSee
text: StockSee is a HackThe6ix-winning data product that links real-world events to stock-price movement with visualization and forecasting. Sachin combined data collection, time-series modelling, NLP sentiment analysis, an explanatory interface, and a deployed web product. The team won the FinTech category, and the project makes market movement easier to explore through real-world event context.

title: MITI collaborative AI music studio
text: MITI is a collaborative AI music studio Sachin built for HackMIT. It combined AI-assisted musical suggestions with a real-time collaborative web experience and won the HackMIT music track. The project demonstrates fast team execution, generative-AI product thinking, full-stack development, and real-time React collaboration.

title: BusForecast
text: BusForecast is a BramHacks-winning project that forecasts event-driven public-transit demand to support surge-bus allocation. Sachin built data collection for upcoming events, attendance prediction using demographic and income data, and a planning interface that highlights high-demand bus routes. The project connects external events to demand modelling and presents the result as a practical civic planning tool.

title: MakeCloud
text: MakeCloud is a natural-language cloud-provisioning assistant Sachin built at UofT Hacks. It translates user intent into Terraform for multi-cloud environments, dynamically creates infrastructure configuration, and makes cloud setup accessible through a conversational interface. It demonstrates agentic developer tooling across Gemini, Python, Flask, React, Terraform, and AWS.

title: QuantRL trading prototype
text: QuantRL is a deep-Q-learning trading system that Sachin built with a custom buy, hold, and sell environment, reward shaping, epsilon decay, and experience replay. In a three-year backtest, it achieved a 191 percent return and improved returns by 27 percent over its baselines. A Flask and React dashboard visualized trades and portfolio performance.

title: ShopFits
text: ShopFits is a Shopify Minis outfit-building project with preference capture, saved looks, sharing, and virtual try-on. Sachin built video try-on and fit-preview features, combining commerce product design, mobile-oriented UI work, and generative and vision-based experimentation.

title: Hackathon and rapid prototyping pattern
text: Sachin repeatedly forms teams and ships working prototypes under short deadlines. He won the HackMIT music track with MITI, the HackThe6ix FinTech category with StockSee, and BramHacks with BusForecast. These projects span generative music, financial data, and transit forecasting, but share the same pattern: identify a concrete user, combine technical components into a usable demo, and communicate the result clearly.

title: Agent and retrieval systems skills
text: Sachin's agent work spans retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, browser automation, planning and memory, tool integration, simulation interfaces, and evaluation. Relevant technologies include LangChain, LangGraph, Pinecone, Neo4j, Google ADK, Codex workflows, DOM-based automation, computer-vision fallback, and LLM evaluation. The strongest evidence comes from Nokia Bell Labs retrieval and recovery agents, InterfaceAI, the Zipline natural-language simulation interface, LearnBridge, and Microsoft's browser-agent testing prototype.

title: Machine-learning systems skills
text: Sachin has experience across ML inference, recommendation systems, model evaluation, streaming data, accelerator kernels, computer vision, forecasting, reinforcement learning, and edge deployment. Technologies and concepts include PyTorch, TensorFlow, Triton Inference Server, Apache Flink, Kafka, GCP, Bigtable, DSPy, AWS Trainium and NKI, object detection, SLAM, LiDAR, and time-series modelling. Evidence is distributed across Shopify production infrastructure, NKI Llama optimization, Nokia Bell Labs research, autonomous drones, StockSee, BusForecast, and QuantRL.

title: Software and systems engineering skills
text: Sachin's software work spans Python, TypeScript and JavaScript, React and Next.js, Flask APIs, Linux, Bash, OpenStack, Terraform, cloud platforms, caching, data pipelines, testing, observability, and simulation. His projects frequently cross layers: infrastructure automation at Nokia, web performance at Microsoft, streaming and caching at Shopify, event simulation at Zipline, and full-stack product prototypes. The common strength is connecting backend or systems behaviour to a usable interface and a measurable operational outcome.

title: Startup and product direction
text: Sachin is exploring AI startup directions where agents and intelligent interfaces reduce friction in real workflows. StoryBook Memoirs is his most emotionally grounded current direction, preserving family stories through conversational interviews and book creation. InterfaceAI represents a developer-productivity and accessibility direction around browser agents. He has also explored real-estate AI. Across these directions, his focus is applied AI systems that turn unstructured context into useful decisions and actions.

title: Interests and community
text: Outside core engineering work, Sachin enjoys hockey goaltending, table tennis, sports, travel, hackathons, and technical community events. These interests add context to his profile and reinforce his preference for team environments, competition, learning in public, and building with others.
